messages:
maya: hey folks — PR <https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/78901|#78901> is up for the 'remote telemetry routing' changes. Need runtime + infra + security eyes before I can schedule a canary. TL;DR: route telemetry to regional collectors, add fallback to local store, small auth header change.

arjun: jumping in — can you summarize perf impact? any increased tail latency expected?

maya: perf numbers in the PR description (small): median token latency +0.4ms, p95 unchanged in our synthetic bench. real-prod will vary. I ran `./scripts/bench/telemetry_latency.sh --runs 50` and attached output.

rachel: @maya thanks — who can own the canary window? I can steward if runtime + infra ok. Also please add a one-line rollback plan in the PR description (what flag to flip).

maya: will add rollback steps. proposed plan: rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2 hours with auto-fallback if error rate > 0.5% over 5min. flag: `telemetry.remote_routing_enabled`.

tony: quick infra note — this touches the VPC egress rules to the regional collector port (tcp/8443). infra acceptance criteria: firewall rule update doc + patch tested on staging. also KMS token refresh handling changed: need to confirm no extra IAM scopes.

infra-bot: CI: integration-tests/telemetry_staging failed (flake) — timeout connecting to collector in 1/3 runs. Re-run suggested.

maya: ack, re-ran integration tests twice: second run passed. I pushed a small retry in the test harness to reduce flakiness and documented it in test/notes.md.

arjun: runtime question — KV cache fallback looks safe, but need to confirm memory accounting for the local store when routing fails. on devices with constrained RAM we should cap to 64MB. can you add `max_local_store_mb: 64` default?

maya: yep will add that config and a note in the config schema.

sec-bot: quick checklist: 1) confirm auth header change preserves existing HMAC signature, 2) add threat model note for routing to external collectors, 3) confirm KMS usage pattern (no long-lived tokens).

maya: 1) HMAC preserved (we append a routing hint after signature header), 2) I added a short threat-model section in the PR, 3) KMS uses short-lived tokens via STS; details in the KMS section of the PR.

tony: can you also include the firewall rule snippet we will apply? paste the `gcloud` command in the PR for infra runbook.

maya: done — added `gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-telemetry-collector --direction=EGRESS --destination-ranges=203.0.113.0/24 --rules=tcp:8443 --network=projects/REDWOOD/global/networks/prod` example and linked to infra runbook.

arjun: I'll run a quick perf smoke test tomorrow morning and post results. if p95 stays within current SLO we can LGTM from runtime side.

rachel: I can take the canary steward role Fri 10–12 PST if that works for runtime + infra.

maya: thanks — requesting formal approvals: @arjun (runtime), @tony (infra), @sec-bot or @sec-team for security signoff, @rachel to own canary.

arjun: ack — leaving a comment with the bench command I ran: `python tools/bench.py --workload telem --duration 300 --concurrency 50`

tony: ok from infra after the firewall snippet and staging smoke pass. small nit: please add a short note about retry backoff (exponential with max 30s) — then infra 👍

maya: added retry backoff note, updated PR. thanks.

sec-bot: security quick signoff pending one doc update: add data-classification row for telemetry payloads. once added I can mark as cleared.

maya: added data-classification row (P2: non-PII operational telemetry). updated PR description.

sec-bot: cleared ✅

arjun: runtime LGTM after perf run. posted results: p50 +0.45ms, p95 +0.9ms (within SLO).

rachel: canary stewarding booked Fri 10–12 PST, I'll start at 5% and follow rollout plan.

maya: thanks all — will merge after approvals settled and schedule the canary with @rachel. planning to merge Thu EOD if no blockers. :thumbsup:
